sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 24.2% a year from $1,702.2 million in FY2016 to $12,001.3 million in FY2025 [F1][F10][F196].
The shape is a step change rather than a smooth ramp: growth ran 46.2% in FY2017 and 49.1% in FY2020, then slowed to 8.9% in FY2025 [D41][D194][D446].
The FY2020 step came from the U.S. launch of TRIKAFTA in the fourth quarter of 2019 and the E.U. launch of KAFTRIO in the third quarter of 2020 [P51].
FY2024 broke the pattern, with operating income of $-232.9 million against $3,832.0 million in FY2023, as $4.6 billion of AIPR&D included $4.4 billion for the Alpine acquisition [F24][F23][P11].
TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO reached $10,312.7 million, or 85.9% of revenue, in FY2025 [S45][D529].
Its contribution to growth collapsed from 13.1pp in FY2024 to 0.7pp in FY2025, while ALYFTREK added 7.6pp on $837.8 million of first-year sales [D528][D531][D590][S69].
The FY2025 top line rose $950.5 million, or 9%, on continued growth in net product revenues [P3].
Operating income grew faster than revenue over the window, at a 95.6% CAGR against 24.2%, but the FY2022..FY2025 operating CAGR is -1.0% [F197][F196][D681].
Diluted EPS of $15.32 in FY2025 compares with $13.89 in FY2023, while the diluted share count was flat at 258.0 million [F75][F73][X137].
The FY2025 operating margin of 34.8% sits above the 31.8% window median but below the 48.2% FY2022 high [F35][D663][D662].
The 36.9pp rebound from FY2024 came mostly from the absence of the prior year's AIPR&D, a 37.7pp residual effect, with SG&A a 1.3pp drag [D452][D468][D467].
Cost of revenue held at 13.8% of revenue in FY2025 as a lower overall royalty rate for the CF medicines offset other costs [D425][P4].
SG&A rose 19.7% in FY2025 after a 28.8% FY2024 increase driven by commercial investment for JOURNAVX and CASGEVY launches [D456][D412][P6].
The FY2025 effective tax rate of 14.9% compares with 315.5% in FY2024, when non-deductible Alpine AIPR&D distorted the rate [D433][D390][P5].
Operating cash flow was $3,631.4 million and free cash flow $3,193.8 million in FY2025, a 26.6% free-cash-flow margin [F85][F105][D431].
Free cash flow covered net income only 0.81x, below the 1.07x window median and the 1.11x peer median [D435][D675][D694].
Operating cash flow of $3.6 billion was primarily due to income from operations of $4.2 billion [P1].
Capex rose 47.0% to $437.6 million, 2.09x D&A and 3.6% of revenue, the highest capital intensity since FY2020 [D447][F95][D436][D430].
Cash and investments of $12,320.4 million against no debt give net cash equal to 102.7% of revenue [D438][D439][D440].
That net cash position ranks at the 88th percentile of eight biopharma peers, whose median is -50.7% of revenue [D691][D692].
Buybacks of $2,017.4 million absorbed 63.2% of FY2025 free cash flow, yet the diluted share count was unchanged at 258.0 million [D441][D442][X137].
The FY2024 cash decline to $11.2 billion was primarily due to the Alpine acquisition and share repurchases [P10].
Days inventory outstanding rose 85 days to 373 in FY2025, the highest in the window and up from 287 in FY2024 [D444][D397][R1].
Inventory of $1,686.8 million now represents 14.1% of revenue, so a demand or write-down issue would hit gross margin directly [X178][F10].
The effective tax rate fell 300.7pp to 14.9% in FY2025 from the distorted 315.5% FY2024 level [D433][D390][R2].
That swing is largely the FY2024 Alpine distortion reversing, so it is a data-quality flag rather than a deterioration [P5].
If TRIKAFTA/KAFTRIO growth stays near the FY2025 0.7% and ALYFTREK does not repeat its 7.6pp contribution, total growth would fall below the 8.9% FY2025 rate [D530][D590][D446].
Watch days inventory outstanding against the FY2025 373 days; a further rise would confirm the build flagged above [D444].
Watch the operating margin against the 31.8% window median; a print below it would reverse the FY2025 recovery [D663][F35].
